newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Coles sees bottom line improvement.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Coles sees bottom line improvement.

text.p: Coles Myer Ltd chairman Nobby Clark said on Tuesday that the company expected the impact of gains in its retail operations to have a positive impact on profits this financial year as long as the upcoming Christmas trading period was reasonable.

"Last year, we achieved some enormous gains behind the scenes in our retail operations. The impact of these gains is not yet evident on our bottom line, but provided we have a reasonable Christmas ahead you should start to see the impact this financial year," Clark said at the annual meeting.

"We do not anticipate any significant lift in retail sales across Austrlaia before mid-1997, but we are working within these constraints to deliver substantial improvements to Coles Myer's performance," Clark also said.
The Melbourne-based company reported a net profit of A$280.4 million in the year to July 28 1996, well below the previous year's record of A$423.4 million.
Clark said the Reserve Bank's recent decision to cut rates half a percentage point was helpful and should support conumser confidence.
"Retailers everywhere are recognising that the customer of the 90s is a complex being, unmoved by many traditional retail offerings, and very much in control of what is now a buyers market."
He said Coles was acutely aware of new customer demands and was "cutting our cloth accordingly".
Coles Myer was looking at its retail brands as a portfolio, Clark said.
"This allows us to more effectively position our brands to meet the wide range of customer preferences and demands that we wish to service," he said. -- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
